Location:

About Exit Mold

Exit Mold is a fast-growing environmental services company specializing in mold and lead inspection, violations management, and remediation coordination. We work closely with property owners, real estate professionals, and contractors to ensure compliance, safety, and efficiency across every project.

We are seeking a highly organized, execution-focused Director of Operations
to partner directly with ownership and drive operational excellence across the business.

Position Overview

The Director of Operations will report directly to the owners and play a critical role in scaling the business. This individual will oversee daily operations, manage internal teams, and build systems that improve efficiency, productivity, and growth.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, understands real estate/property operations, and enjoys building structure within growing businesses.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership

Oversee all day-to-day office operations, ensuring smooth execution across teams

Manage and support a team of 12–14 inspectors, ensuring productivity and accountability

Act as the central point of contact for operational questions, escalations, and problem-solving

Handle issues proactively in a calm, professional, and solutions-oriented manner

Scheduling & Workflow Management

Oversee incoming calls, bookings, and technical inquiries related to violations

Ensure efficient scheduling and time management across all employees and inspectors

Monitor daily workflows to ensure timely completion of tasks and services

Process Improvement & Systems Development

Build, implement, and optimize operational systems and processes

Conduct ongoing process analysis to identify inefficiencies and implement improvements

Develop scalable workflows to support company growth while minimizing costs

Identify barriers to execution and recommend actionable solutions

Strategy & Growth

Partner with ownership to develop and execute operational strategies

Help drive expansion efforts across New York and New Jersey

Develop long-term plans to improve productivity, service delivery, and profitability

Team Development & Performance Management

Collaborate with ownership to establish employee performance goals and KPIs

Monitor performance metrics and ensure accountability across the team

Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performance work environment

Industry Expertise & Compliance

Become an expert in NYC mold and lead regulations, violations, and reporting requirements

Ensure all operations comply with local NYC laws, regulations, and company policies

Work closely with external partners, subcontractors, and stakeholders

Data & Metrics

Track, analyze, and report on key operational metrics

Use data to drive decision-making and improve efficiency

Qualifications

5–10+ years of operations experience, preferably in real estate, property management, construction, or home services

Experience coordinating or supporting HPD and/or DOH violations, compliance, or remediation projects is preferred.

Familiarity with mold, lead, asbestos, or other environmental compliance requirements is a plus.

Proven ability to manage teams and improve operational processes

Strong organizational and problem-solving skills

Experience building systems and scaling operations in a growing business

Comfortable working in a fast-paced, hands-on environment

Strong communication and leadership skills

Experience managing scheduling, field teams, or service-based operations is highly preferred

What We’re Looking For

A true operator who enjoys execution, not just strategy

Someone who can bring structure and accountability to a growing business

A leader who can balance people management with process improvement

A proactive problem-solver who takes ownership and drives results

Why Join Exit Mold

Direct access to ownership and real impact on company growth

Opportunity to build and scale operations from the ground up

Fast-growing company with strong market demand

High visibility role with long-term growth potential

EXECUTIVE VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT

OZARKS REGIONAL YMCA

Position:
Chief Executive Officer

Address:
323 N Patton Ave, Springfield, MO 65806

Website:

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Ozarks Regional YMCA is seeking a visionary, mission-driven leader to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer. This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a respected, multi-branch YMCA association with a proud 137-year history of strengthening communities across Southwest Missouri.

The organization enters its next chapter from a position of renewed strength. Through focused leadership and the commitment of an engaged board and dedicated staff team, the YMCA has strengthened operations, improved organizational stability, and established a clear strategic direction for future growth. The next CEO will have the opportunity to build upon this momentum while expanding the YMCA's impact throughout the region.

Serving nearly 20,000 members through multiple branches, childcare programs, camps, and community initiatives, the Ozarks Regional YMCA is uniquely positioned to address some of the region's most pressing needs, including youth development, affordable childcare, water safety, chronic disease prevention, and community well-being.

The Board of Directors seeks a collaborative and strategic leader who will inspire others, build meaningful partnerships, strengthen philanthropic support, and elevate the YMCA's visibility as one of the region's leading nonprofit organizations. The successful candidate will possess the vision to identify emerging opportunities, the operational expertise to execute effectively, and the relationship-building skills necessary to unite stakeholders around a shared vision for community impact.

Above all, the CEO will champion a culture rooted in the YMCA's mission, values, and unwavering commitment to youth protection. The safety and well-being of children will remain central to every decision, program, and interaction across the association.

WHY THIS LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY MATTERS

The next CEO will join the Ozarks Regional YMCA at a pivotal and exciting moment in its history. Key opportunities include:

Leading the implementation of an ambitious strategic vision focused on childcare access, water safety, health improvement, and community connection.
Advancing a proposed $6 million capital development initiative designed to expand community impact and enhance recreational opportunities for families throughout the region.
Building upon a strong foundation of community trust while elevating the YMCA's role as a leading convener, collaborator, and advocate for healthy communities.
Strengthening long-term financial sustainability through philanthropy, earned revenue growth, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.
Developing and empowering the next generation of YMCA leaders while fostering a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
For an accomplished executive seeking meaningful work and the opportunity to create lasting impact, the Ozarks Regional YMCA offers both a significant leadership challenge and an extraordinary platform for community transformation.

Key Skills And Abilities Of Our Next Ceo

The board believes its new CEO should be an experienced leader who has the background and qualities that will permit him or her to achieve excellence in the following roles:

Implement the Vision and Strategic Priorities:
Collaborate effectively with volunteers, community leaders, and key staff to develop and execute a strategic plan that addresses the evolving needs of the communities served by the Y. Ensure the plan includes clearly defined organizational strategies, actionable implementation steps, measurable outcomes, and accountability for results. Key competencies: Change Leadership, Communication & Influence, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Program/Project Management

Improve Operating Performance:
Partner with the board and staff leadership to develop and implement an annual operational plan that advances organizational goals while promoting safe, relevant, and sustainable practices. Proactively identify and address challenges, anticipate future needs, and provide effective oversight of the Y’s operations, programs, and services. Key competencies: Developing Self & Others, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Innovation

Fiscal Management:
Apply advanced financial analysis and forecasting to support the organization’s long-term growth, stability, and sustainability. Consistently lead the Y toward balanced or surplus operations through revenue growth, philanthropic support, and prudent cost management. Empower and support staff leaders in achieving strong financial performance within their areas of responsibility, while developing and implementing effective stewardship strategies. Key competencies: Fiscal Management, Critical Thinking & Decision Making, Developing Self & Others, Philanthropy

Position the Y as a Vital Partner for Community Change:
Serve as a visible and credible ambassador for the YMCA’s mission, vision, and values throughout the community. Build and strengthen relationships with diverse stakeholders, community partners, and civic leaders while consistently demonstrating the highest standards of integrity and service. Ensure the Y is recognized as a leading nonprofit dedicated to strengthening communities by connecting people to their potential, purpose, and one another. Key competencies: Communication & Influence, Engaging Community, Collaboration

Steward Fundraising Efforts:
Develop and execute a comprehensive annual fundraising strategy that engages members, volunteers, staff, donors, and community partners in advancing the YMCA’s mission. Assess and pursue opportunities for capital development while expanding the organization’s effectiveness and impact in annual giving, major gifts, and endowment growth. Key competencies: Philanthropy, Engaging Community, Communication & Influence

Lead a High-Performing Team:
Develop and implement a comprehensive talent development strategy that promotes a supportive, inclusive, and culturally competent workplace. Recruit, develop, and retain a diverse and high-performing team that reflects and serves the community. Foster a culture of collaboration, shared accountability, continuous learning, and leadership development across the organization. Key competencies: Developing Self & Others, Inclusion, Emotional Maturity, Change Leadership

ASSOCIATION SNAPSHOT

The Ozarks Regional YMCA is a long-standing nonprofit organization based in Southwest Missouri, founded in Springfield in 1888, with a mission centered on strengthening community through inclusive programs and services. Rooted in Christian principles, the organization focuses on building healthy spirit, mind, and body for all people, regardless of age, background, or financial situation.

The Ozarks Regional YMCA is supported by a strong, mission-driven staff team in partnership with the board committed to serving the diverse needs of the communities across its service area. Staff and leadership bring a blend of experience, collaboration, and passion for youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. With a culture that emphasizes teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement, the organization is well-positioned to deliver high-quality programs and services. The strength of the team is reflected in its ability to adapt, innovate, and build meaningful relationships that advance the YMCA’s impact throughout the region.

The Ozarks Regional YMCA continues to reflect a commitment to excellence in everything we do. We focus our work in three key areas of impact, because nurturing the potential of children, helping people live healthier and supporting our neighbors are fundamental to strengthening communities. We believe that to bring about meaningful change in individuals and communities, we must be focused and accountable.

Through its network of family centers, camps, and community initiatives, the YMCA provides opportunities for youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility, offering programs such as childcare, sports, wellness activities, and community outreach. With a strong commitment to accessibility, the Ozarks Regional YMCA also provides financial assistance to ensure that everyone has the opportunity to learn, grow, and thrive, making it a vital resource for individuals and families across the region.

Position Summary

Under the general direction of the Chief Operating Office, the District, Executive Director has the responsibilities and accountability to successfully lead and manage multiple branch operations and implement the policies and programs of the YMCA of Greater Cleveland. This position is accountable for the day to day operations of all assigned YMCA facilities.

Responsibilities includes overall accountability for district operations for all assigned facilities, while also providing leadership to branch board development; branch fiscal management; branch fundraising/annual campaign; branch director selection, member engagement, community engagement, property management; and the carrying out of our Association's strategic plan. The position may also have the responsibility to lead and/or direct Association-Wide initiatives/priorities, programs and strategies.

Because this position is responsible for multiple operational sites, the initiation of timely communication among the branch staff, Association staff, and boards regarding the status of goals and overall operations is critical.

Serves and performs the duties of Executive Director at assigned branch.
Provides leadership and support to associate/branch executive directors within own district to ensure operational and financial targets are met.
Identifies potential areas for branch cooperative programming to accomplish YMCA goals, and works with staff groups to develop and implement programs.
Assists branch staff in the planning, development and implementation of new program initiatives and activities.
Provides leadership and support to the branches to ensure quality, safety and sustainability of branch operations.
Provides leadership and support to the branch executive directors to ensure that fundraising targets are met. In conjunction with association leadership team and branch executives, develops annual membership goals and conducts branch reviews for evaluation of execution.
In cooperation with the CFO and COO leads the preparation and management of branch budgets in assigned districts.

The next Executive Director will step into an organization with deep community roots and a dedicated staff, with the support of a Board committed to strengthening LAC's operational and financial foundation for the next generation of impact.

Mission:
To promote the integration, well-being, and full participation of immigrant and Latino families in Charlotte and the surrounding region.

Reporting Structure
: The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and leads a team of approximately 12 staff and contractors, directly supervising a six-person senior management team spanning operations, finance, and program leadership.

Total Staff and Budget
: Approximately 12 staff members and contractors; annual operating budget of $1.9 million.

Salary

Working Environment/Location:
This is a full-time, in-person position based in Charlotte, North Carolina. Relocation assistance is not provided.

Financial Management & Organizational Effectiveness
Develop and implement a financial stabilization and sustainability plan, including cash flow management, budgeting, forecasting, financial controls, and risk management.
Develop and administer the annual operating budget and pursue Board approval.
Ensure compliance with all financial reporting requirements, audits, grant agreements, government contracts, and applicable regulations.
Strengthen existing programs and organizational capacity to advance mission impact on a stable and sustainable financial foundation

Operational Effectiveness, Strategic Leadership & Change Management

Direct the day-to-day operations of the organization to ensure efficient, effective, mission-driven service delivery.

Ensure that organizational decisions are informed by data, community needs, and measurable outcomes.

About the Center for Health Policy and Law:

The Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL), “The Center” promotes innovative solutions to public health challenges at home and around the globe. The Center advances law and policy reforms to strengthen population health, reduce health disparities, nourish public health programs, and enhance access to affordable, high-quality healthcare. Housed in the School of Law and firmly rooted in Northeastern University’s nine academic colleges and international network of campuses, the Center brings together Northeastern faculty, students, and experts across disciplines to share knowledge; conduct and disseminate research; and influence the formulation and implementation of health policy and law.

About the Salus Populi:

Salus Populi: Educating the Judiciary about the Social Determinants of Health (SP) is a project in collaboration with the Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL) at Northeastern University School of Law and the Institute for Health Equity and Social Justice Research (Institute) at Northeastern University that seeks to provide guidance and training to judges and lawyers on the impact of the law on the social determinants of health (SDOH). Funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) and the Kellogg Foundation (Kellogg), CHPL has received grants to train judges about the SDOH, with the goal of moving judges to render decisions that support health equity. The program also trains lawyers and other court personnels. The SP judicial education program is a tuition-free, interactive, and discussion-oriented course that provides judges with the tools they need to recognize how the SDOH impact the issues that come before courts and to read and evaluate public health research relating to the SDOH. The program is offered in Boston and virtually, and other locations with local partners, like San Francisco, Cleveland and North Dakota.
Since its start, SP has trained over 2100 attendees from all over the country. The team consists of faculty and staff from both CHPL and the Institute.

Position Summary:

CHPL is seeking a Program Director to oversee projects and deliverables within the Salus Populi (SP) portfolio. This position operates on a hybrid schedule, requiring some in-person days on the Boston campus.

The Program Director will have overall responsibility for the daily functioning of the SP program and work with other members of the SP Leadership team on all aspects of program development and implementation. The Program Director will be responsible for creating and implementing curriculum, organizing events, supervising program staff, and fostering collaboration partnerships. The Program Director will manage the budget and support the development of grant proposals, facilitate meetings, organize events, present at conferences, work with external partners, supervise staff, supervise law students and be adept at project management. The Program Director will serve the mission of SP by helping to train judges, lawyers and other court personnel on the SDOH. We are looking for an attorney who wants to be part of a team that has a passion for health equity, public health policy and law.

Continuation of the appointment beyond 11/1/27 is anticipated but remains contingent upon funding availability

JD or equivalent degree and at least 3 years of relevant work experience (e.g. higher education, public health, nonprofit, legal practice, government).
Extensive knowledge of public health law and health policy.
Demonstrated commitment to health equity and belonging and the ability to work with a diverse group of students, staff, and faculty.
Strong attention to detail and proven ability to successfully plan, execute, and monitor complex projects with multiple stakeholders and deliverables.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, this includes the ability to facilitate meetings, conduct presentations and draft reports and legal arguments.
Must be self-directed, able to make independent decisions.

Strategic Leadership and Supervision

Serve as a mentor and supervisor for staff, student interns and research assistants, fostering their growth and development within the organization
Coordinate communications for the project

Organizational Management

Supervise the legal research and drafting activities and deliverables for the project in collaboration with the project’s Principal Investigator

Research and draft academic papers and other deliverables;

Serve as a course instructor for most of the Salus Populi judicial and legal education program sessions.

BAE Systems Intelligence & Security (I&S) is seeking a Sr. Director of Strategic Partnerships to lead and elevate our relationships with key technology partners—beginning with one flagship partner and expanding across a portfolio of emerging and mid-tier technology innovators. This is not a passive alliance management role. We are building a partnership engine that materially shapes our market position, capture strategy, solution offerings, and long-term competitive differentiation.

We need a leader who sees around corners, operates with executive presence, and blends the DNA of two worlds:

Modern technology companies
Large defense primes or national security organizations

If you've sat on both sides of that table, understand how value flows across ecosystems, and know how to turn partnerships into measurable business impact—you’ll thrive here.

Who You Are

A relationship-driven strategist with deep operational discipline. A builder who treats partnerships as strategic assets—not marketing logos. Someone who can translate between goals, roadmaps, projects and outcomes leveraging relationships not authority to drive success.

You Are

Forward-leaning and innovative
Disciplined and organized
Fluent in both commercial technology and defense culture
Credible with senior executives in both domains
Comfortable driving outcomes without authority
Highly collaborative across Business Leadership, Business Development, Technology, and Contracting

Opportunity

The Sr. Director of Strategic Partnerships will lead the execution for our highest-priority technology partnership while also architecting a repeatable partnerships model for the entire sector. This role reports to the Chief Innovation & Strategy Officer and regular will engage with senior sector executive leadership as well as leadership of our key partners. The opportunity is to shepherd accelerated technology adoption, expand jointly addressable markets, and drive differentiated offerings into pursuits and programs.

You Will Shape

Our joint technology strategies
How we integrate commercial capabilities into mission systems
How we shape our roadmaps in concert with partners
How we co-create differentiators for major captures
How we expand cross-organization engagement models and governance
How we turn relationships into strategic wins

Conduct ongoing analysis of partner ecosystems, technology shifts, competitive alliances, and whitespace opportunities.
Create partnership “win strategies” aligned to capture, solution architecture, and enterprise transformation priorities.

Drive Business Impact

Translate partnerships into measurable outcomes: pipeline acceleration, capture discriminators, solution enhancements, and program performance improvements.
Shape major pursuits by integrating partner capabilities into technical solutions, price-to-win strategies, and evaluation-aligned narratives.
Identify areas where partners can unlock mission value through AI/ML, cloud, modeling/simulation, data architectures, DevSecOps accelerators, and other next-gen technologies.

Build partnership playbooks, templates, and engagement mechanisms that scale across additional technology partners.

You’ve delivered results by turning partnerships into material business wins.

Adaptive strategist — You thrive in evolving acquisition landscapes (OTAs, prototype-first pathways, accelerated timelines).
Continuous learner — You stay ahead of both commercial and defense tech trends, partner ecosystem shifts, and mission needs.

Competitive drive with a bias for action.
Intellectual honesty and transparency in representing risks and opportunities.
Relationship-oriented leadership grounded in competence and respect.
Mission-focused mindset—everything connects to customer and warfighter impact.

Demonstrated track record influencing senior executives and shaping business outcomes across complex organizations.

Certifications such as PMP or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt.

Direct experience with multi-level terminal design, advanced baggage handling systems, people-mover integration, and sustainable airport design.
Experience leading phased construction programs that protected continuing operations at a hub airport without disruption to airline schedules or passenger experience.

About the Center for Health Policy and Law:

The Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL), “The Center” promotes innovative solutions to public health challenges at home and around the globe. The Center advances law and policy reforms to strengthen population health, reduce health disparities, nourish public health programs, and enhance access to affordable, high-quality healthcare. Housed in the School of Law and firmly rooted in Northeastern University’s nine academic colleges and international network of campuses, the Center brings together Northeastern faculty, students, and experts across disciplines to share knowledge; conduct and disseminate research; and influence the formulation and implementation of health policy and law.

About the Salus Populi:

Salus Populi: Educating the Judiciary about the Social Determinants of Health (SP) is a project in collaboration with the Center for Health Policy and Law (CHPL) at Northeastern University School of Law and the Institute for Health Equity and Social Justice Research (Institute) at Northeastern University that seeks to provide guidance and training to judges and lawyers on the impact of the law on the social determinants of health (SDOH). Funded by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF) and the Kellogg Foundation (Kellogg), CHPL has received grants to train judges about the SDOH, with the goal of moving judges to render decisions that support health equity. The program also trains lawyers and other court personnels. The SP judicial education program is a tuition-free, interactive, and discussion-oriented course that provides judges with the tools they need to recognize how the SDOH impact the issues that come before courts and to read and evaluate public health research relating to the SDOH. The program is offered in Boston and virtually, and other locations with local partners, like San Francisco, Cleveland and North Dakota.
Since its start, SP has trained over 2100 attendees from all over the country. The team consists of faculty and staff from both CHPL and the Institute.

Position Summary:

CHPL is seeking a Program Director to oversee projects and deliverables within the Salus Populi (SP) portfolio. This position operates on a hybrid schedule, requiring some in-person days on the Boston campus.

The Program Director will have overall responsibility for the daily functioning of the SP program and work with other members of the SP Leadership team on all aspects of program development and implementation. The Program Director will be responsible for creating and implementing curriculum, organizing events, supervising program staff, and fostering collaboration partnerships. The Program Director will manage the budget and support the development of grant proposals, facilitate meetings, organize events, present at conferences, work with external partners, supervise staff, supervise law students and be adept at project management. The Program Director will serve the mission of SP by helping to train judges, lawyers and other court personnel on the SDOH. We are looking for an attorney who wants to be part of a team that has a passion for health equity, public health policy and law.

Continuation of the appointment beyond 11/1/27 is anticipated but remains contingent upon funding availability

BAE Systems Intelligence & Security (I&S) is seeking a Sr. Director of Strategic Partnerships to lead and elevate our relationships with key technology partners—beginning with one flagship partner and expanding across a portfolio of emerging and mid-tier technology innovators. This is not a passive alliance management role. We are building a partnership engine that materially shapes our market position, capture strategy, solution offerings, and long-term competitive differentiation.

We need a leader who sees around corners, operates with executive presence, and blends the DNA of two worlds:

Modern technology companies
Large defense primes or national security organizations

If you've sat on both sides of that table, understand how value flows across ecosystems, and know how to turn partnerships into measurable business impact—you’ll thrive here.

Who You Are

A relationship-driven strategist with deep operational discipline. A builder who treats partnerships as strategic assets—not marketing logos. Someone who can translate between goals, roadmaps, projects and outcomes leveraging relationships not authority to drive success.

You Are

Forward-leaning and innovative
Disciplined and organized
Fluent in both commercial technology and defense culture
Credible with senior executives in both domains
Comfortable driving outcomes without authority
Highly collaborative across Business Leadership, Business Development, Technology, and Contracting

Opportunity

The Sr. Director of Strategic Partnerships will lead the execution for our highest-priority technology partnership while also architecting a repeatable partnerships model for the entire sector. This role reports to the Chief Innovation & Strategy Officer and regular will engage with senior sector executive leadership as well as leadership of our key partners. The opportunity is to shepherd accelerated technology adoption, expand jointly addressable markets, and drive differentiated offerings into pursuits and programs.

You Will Shape

Our joint technology strategies
How we integrate commercial capabilities into mission systems
How we shape our roadmaps in concert with partners
How we co-create differentiators for major captures
How we expand cross-organization engagement models and governance
How we turn relationships into strategic wins

Partnership Development Responsibilities

Build and execute the multi-year strategy for our primary technology partner—including joint value propositions, market alignment, and investment areas.
Assess and manage a portfolio of smaller tech partners, including prioritization, tiering, and resource allocation.
Conduct ongoing analysis of partner ecosystems, technology shifts, competitive alliances, and whitespace opportunities.
Create partnership “win strategies” aligned to capture, solution architecture, and enterprise transformation priorities.

Drive Business Impact

Translate partnerships into measurable outcomes: pipeline acceleration, capture discriminators, solution enhancements, and program performance improvements.
Shape major pursuits by integrating partner capabilities into technical solutions, price-to-win strategies, and evaluation-aligned narratives.
Identify areas where partners can unlock mission value through AI/ML, cloud, modeling/simulation, data architectures, DevSecOps accelerators, and other next-gen technologies.

Relationship Development & Executive Engagement

Act as the primary executive interface with partner leadership teams—managing rhythms, governance, strategic planning, and conflict resolution.
Develop trusted relationships across technology, business winning, partner management, and delivery organizations on both sides.

Operationalize & Scale the Partnership Model

Establish governance structures (QBRs, tech syncs, roadmap exchanges, co-invest processes, and data-sharing workflows).
Ensure compliance with security, data exchange, and export control constraints.
Build partnership playbooks, templates, and engagement mechanisms that scale across additional technology partners.
Lead internal cross-functional working groups to ensure alignment across Business Winning, Solutions Architecture, Technology, Contracts, Legal and Programs.

Communicate with Authority

Craft compelling written materials that communicate strategic intent, capture value, and influence decision-makers.

A Winning Track Record — Required This role requires more than partnership maintenance—it requires proof of impact.

You’ve delivered results by turning partnerships into material business wins.
You’ve shaped competitive outcomes—joint captures, product integrations, or mission-focused solutions.
You understand how both government evaluators and commercial partner ecosystems operate, and you design strategies that resonate with both.
You've learned from misses, incorporated feedback, and improved partnership strategies accordingly.

A Modern Mindset

AI-fluent — You use and understand modern AI tools (LLMs, copilots, automation platforms) and apply them to partnership workflows, joint solutioning, and competitive strategy.
Adaptive strategist — You thrive in evolving acquisition landscapes (OTAs, prototype-first pathways, accelerated timelines).
Continuous learner — You stay ahead of both commercial and defense tech trends, partner ecosystem shifts, and mission needs.

Character

Competitive drive with a bias for action.
Intellectual honesty and transparency in representing risks and opportunities.
Relationship-oriented leadership grounded in competence and respect.
Mission-focused mindset—everything connects to customer and warfighter impact.

Core Competencies

Strategic Alignment — Connect day-to-day operations with the broader security and innovation roadmap.
Operational Rigor — Build repeatable processes, maintain high-fidelity data, and promote governance excellence.
Detail Orientation — Ensure accuracy in time tracking, financial stewardship, and multi-source data aggregation.
Analytical Thinking — Identify bottlenecks early, surface root causes, and propose actionable solutions.
Collaboration — Build trusted relationships across technical, product, and executive teams.
Integrity & Confidentiality — Uphold strong standards in the handling of sensitive or controlled information.
Curiosity & Creativity – Bring a sense of curiosity for innovation, improving how we serve the enterprise backed by a sense of creativity and willingness to lean in.

15+ years in technology, defense, or dual-industry roles spanning partnerships, strategy, solutions, BD, or engineering leadership.
Proven success leading strategic alliances or enterprise-level partner relationships with major technology companies (e.g., Microsoft, AWS, Google, Palantir).
Experience working within or closely alongside a large defense prime or major federal integrator—deep familiarity with DoD, IC, and national security missions.
Strong understanding of cloud architectures, AI/ML ecosystems, enterprise software, open architectures, and modern engineering practices.
Demonstrated track record influencing senior executives and shaping business outcomes across complex organizations.
Exceptional organizational discipline; able to manage ambiguity, multiple stakeholders, and cross-functional initiatives.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance.
Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred

Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills

Experience in an Innovation Lab, Corporate R&D, Cybersecurity Program Office, or a Corporate Strategy environment.
Certifications such as PMP or Lean Six Sigma Green Belt.
Familiarity with engineering workflow tools (Jira).

However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
